findings.reason: The original standalone tile contains the disc definition and section-length computation but no picture. A concrete vertical slice materially clarifies why the interval has two square-root endpoints and why its length is the Cavalieri integrand. This is warranted exposition even though the existing proof is complete.

diagram_math_checks.data: Open unit disc D and boundary x^2+y^2=1
diagram_math_checks.check: Example line 24 defines D by strict inequality; the circle is dashed and the caption explicitly excludes it. Axis intercepts ±1 agree with the defining equation.

Verification step 1.1 gives D_x=(-sqrt(1-x^2),sqrt(1-x^2)). The sketch uses x=0.5 and y approximately ±sqrt(3)/2, labels those endpoints symbolically at x_0, and marks them open. No endpoints are included in D.
Upper minus lower endpoint is sqrt(1-x_0^2)-(-sqrt(1-x_0^2))=2sqrt(1-x_0^2), precisely the length and integrand in Verification step 1.1. The arrow spans the same two heights.

The caption restricts the illustrated representative to 0<x_0<1; it makes no claim of a nonempty section at x=±1 or beyond. Step 1.1 continues to give empty sections outside [-1,1], with endpoint intervals (0,0) empty as well.

diagram_math_checks.data: Excluded section endpoints: corrected visible convention
diagram_math_checks.check: The strict inequality in Example line 24 and open interval in Verification step 1.1 exclude the two endpoints. Both revised SVG subpaths have fill="var(--background, transparent)", stroke="var(--tikz-blue, #00f)", stroke-width=".7", radius 3.442 SVG units. Fresh native original-resolution inspection shows dark interiors with visible rings, matching endpoint exclusion. The labels, section coordinates and length relation are unchanged.
